title: IIS with MathOpt, gurobipy and Pyomo

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A model has two separate conflicts, {budget_2029, must_P5} and {crew_2030, force_P8}. A deletion filter tests the rows in the order must_P5, budget_2029, crew_2030, force_P8. Which conflict does it return?

options.text: {budget_2029, must_P5}, since it tests those two rows first
options.says: Rows tested first are dropped while the other conflict still holds without them.

options.text: {crew_2030, force_P8}, since it tests those two rows last
options.says: Right: must_P5 and budget_2029 go while the second conflict keeps the rest infeasible.

options.text: All four rows, since both conflicts are present in the model
options.says: Each answer is irreducible; four rows with two separate conflicts are not.

options.text: The smaller conflict, since the filter returns the smallest IIS
options.says: A deletion filter returns an irreducible set, not the smallest; order decides.

origin.section: The Deletion Filter Keeps the Conflict It Tests Last

questions.stem: Gurobi's computeIIS returns 6 rows and 25 variable bounds. Your deletion filter, which never touches bounds, returns 4 rows. Both are irreducible. What explains the difference?

options.text: One of them is wrong, since every model has exactly one IIS to find
options.says: A model can have many IISs; the Budget Lock scenario has several.

options.text: Gurobi's is wrong, since an IIS should hold rows only and never bounds
options.says: Bounds are constraints too, and Gurobi's IIS may include them.

options.text: They are two IISs, since Gurobi may keep a row where a bound would do
options.says: Right: with every bound forced in, Gurobi returned the filter's four rows.

options.text: Gurobi solved the LP relaxation, since computeIIS drops integrality
options.says: computeIIS works on the MIP; the relaxation needs model.relax() first.

origin.section: computeIIS Counts Variable Bounds as Members

questions.stem: A must-do job needs 13 crew-months in its start year, 2030 or 2031, and each year has 12. Pyomo's MIS tool, run with HiGHS, says the model is feasible. Why?

options.text: The tool solves the LP relaxation, where half the job each year fits
options.says: Right: the tool sets every variable's domain to the reals, and 6.5 crew-months fit in 12.

options.text: The tool skips the must-do rows, which it turns into variable bounds
options.says: It turns variable bounds into rows; it does not skip any row.

options.text: HiGHS rounds the crew rows, which hides the single crew-month short
options.says: HiGHS solved what it was given; the relaxed model really is feasible.

options.text: The rows really are feasible, which a MILP solve would also show
options.says: The MILP is infeasible: Gurobi's IIS names these three rows.

origin.section: Pyomo: write_iis Asks Gurobi, the MIS Tool Solves the LP Relaxation
